title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
title_zh: 人类活动对新发传染病的痕迹
abstract: Abstract Emerging infectious diseases are a hallmark of the Anthropocene 1,2 . Human-driven ecosystem changes and human–wildlife–livestock contact can drive the emergence of zoonotic and vector-borne diseases 3–5 , but how much these processes shape landscapes of outbreak risk is poorly understood, beyond a few well-studied systems 6–8 . Here we consolidate 58,319 outbreak event records for 32 diseases and systematically test how 16 hypothesized social and environmental drivers impact outbreak geographies, while accounting for detection and reporting biases. We show that outbreak risks are typically highest in mosaic landscapes where people and livestock live alongside forests and fragmented ecosystems. These combined factors, along with long-term declines in precipitation, share strong impacts across several vector-borne diseases (for example, dengue, Lyme disease and zoonotic arboviruses). By contrast, directly transmitted zoonoses (for example, Ebola and mpox) share few common drivers, and the impacts of most other anthropogenic pressures (for example, deforestation, climate warming and agricultural intensification) vary widely between diseases. Most consistently, the observed geography of outbreaks is shaped by healthcare access: reporting declines by a median of 32% (range across diseases: 1.2–96.7%) for each additional hour’s travel time from a health facility. Our findings underscore that infectious disease spillover and emergence are multi-causal, and that no one-size-fits-all strategy can prevent epidemics and pandemics. Ecosystem-based public health interventions 9 should always follow system-specific evidence, and be paired with greater investment in health systems and One Health pathogen surveillance.
abstract_zh: 摘要 新发传染病是人类世的标志1,2。人类驱动的生态系统变化以及人与野生动物、家畜的接触可促成人畜共患病和媒介传播疾病的出现3–5，但这些过程在多大程度上塑造了疫情风险景观仍不清楚，除了一些已被充分研究的系统6–8。本文汇总了32种疾病的58,319起疫情事件记录，并系统检验了16种假设的社会和环境驱动因素对疫情地理分布的影响，同时考虑了检测和报告偏差。结果显示，疫情风险通常在混合景观中最高，即人类和家畜与森林及碎片化生态系统共存的地区。这些因素与长期降水量下降共同对多种媒介传播疾病（如登革热、莱姆病和人畜共患的虫媒病毒）产生强烈影响。相反，直接传播的人畜共患病（如埃博拉和猴痘）共享的驱动因素很少，其他大多数人类活动压力（如森林砍伐、气候变暖和农业集约化）的影响在不同疾病之间差异很大。最为一致的是，疫情地理分布受医疗服务可及性影响：每增加一小时从医疗机构的行程时间，报告率中位下降32%（各疾病范围：1.2–96.7%）。我们的发现强调，传染病的溢出和出现是多因性的，没有一种通用策略能预防流行病和大流行。基于生态系统的公共卫生干预9应始终遵循系统特定的证据，并与对卫生系统和“一体化健康”病原体监测的更大投入相结合。
